note: P0 starter catalog. Read tools run freely; mutating tools require an approved plan. Expanded to full coverage in P4.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Get a live snapshot of the rig: equipment connection, current capture/sequence/plan progress, guider RMS, live-stack frame count, focus, meridian time-to-flip. Use this to answer 'how is it going' or before proposing a correction.

tools.name: get_tonights_best
tools.description: List tonight's best deep-sky targets (plus Moon/planets/comets) observable from the user's location and time window, ranked. Use when the user asks what to shoot.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Find a deep-sky object by name or catalog id (e.g. M16, NGC 7000, Eagle Nebula) and get its coordinates and metadata.

tools.name: get_altitude
tools.description: Get the altitude track of a target across the night for the user's location, to judge when it's high enough and for how long.

tools.name: get_weather
tools.description: Get the 3-day astronomy weather forecast (3h slots) with cloud/seeing/transparency and an observation score for the user's site. Use for planning and for deciding mid-session route changes.

tools.name: slew_to
tools.description: Slew the mount to coordinates and plate-solve-center on them. MUTATES: moves the telescope. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: run_autofocus
tools.description: Start an automated V-curve autofocus run on the selected optical train. MUTATES: moves the focuser and captures. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: start_live_stack
tools.description: Start live (EAA) stacking with the given exposure and gain. MUTATES: begins capturing. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: start_plan
tools.description: Start a saved multi-target night plan by id. MUTATES: runs a whole automated session. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: List the user's saved multi-target night plans (PLAN mode library) with their ids, target names, and frame lists. Use to see what's already saved before building or starting one.

tools.name: create_plan
tools.description: Build a multi-target night plan in PLAN mode from your target suggestions and save it to the user's plan library. This only saves a reviewable DRAFT — nothing moves and no capture starts; the user reviews/edits it in the PLAN tab and presses Start themselves (that is the separate start_plan tool, which needs approval). Get each target's J2000 coordinates first via search_catalog or get_tonights_best. After creating, call show_panel with tab 'plan' so the user can see it. Returns the saved plan including its new id.

name.description: Plan name, e.g. 'Jul 5 - Veil + North America'.

targets.description: Targets imaged in order. Each needs J2000 coordinates and a frame list.

raHours.description: J2000 right ascension in decimal HOURS.

thumbKey.description: Catalog slug like 'M42' or 'NGC7000' for the UI preview thumbnail; optional.

frames.description: Exposure blocks captured for this target.

filter.description: Filter name, if a filter wheel is used (e.g. 'Ha', 'L', 'R'); omit for OSC.

gain.description: Camera gain; omit to use the current setting.

ditherEveryNFrames.description: Dither via the guider every N frames (0 = off).

refocusEveryNFrames.description: Auto-focus every N frames (0 = off; needs a focuser).

autoFocusOnStart.description: Run one auto-focus pass at the start of the plan (needs a focuser).

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the assistant's knowledge base, which covers BOTH general astrophotography best-practice (focusing, guiding, exposure/gain/histogram, light pollution & filters, polar alignment, calibration frames, planning & targets, diagnosing bad subs) AND the full N.I.N.A. Polaris user manual — every tab, workflow, setting and button. Use it whenever the user asks 'how do I / where is / what does this do / why', or seems lost or confused, whether the question is general technique or product-specific (which screen to open, how a Polaris feature works, what a setting means, fixing an error message). Base your answer on the returned passages (each has a `source` like 'polaris/live-stacking' or 'focusing'); if the answer is about a screen, also call show_panel to take the user there. If nothing relevant comes back, answer from general knowledge and say so.

query.description: What to look up, e.g. 'why are my stars elongated in the corners' or 'how long should narrowband subs be'.

tools.name: show_panel
tools.description: Switch the Polaris UI to a panel so the user sees what you're doing or reviewing (e.g. FOCUS while adjusting focus, LIVE to show the stack, PLAN to review the night). Non-destructive; use freely to guide the user.

tools.name: analyze_frame
tools.description: Capture the current camera frame (what the user is viewing in LIVE/PREVIEW/AUTORUN) and visually inspect it. Use when the user asks whether an image looks good, to diagnose a problem, or to check focus, star shape, tracking/trailing, gradients/light pollution, satellites/planes, or framing. The frame is attached as an image right after this call so you can look at it directly, then give a short verdict and any fix.

tools.name: analyze_selected_frame
tools.description: Visually inspect the frame the user has selected in the STUDIO Files browser (a saved FITS/image on disk) and give a short verdict (depth, gradients, star shape, framing, focus, trailing) plus any fix. Use this whenever the user asks about 'this frame', 'the selected file/image', or 'the one I picked in Files' — you do NOT need to ask them to open it; the selected frame is attached as an image right after this call. Works when exactly one file is selected in the Files tab.

tools.name: analyze_current_view
tools.description: Look at the image the user is CURRENTLY viewing in Polaris — whatever panel happens to be selected (LIVE, PREVIEW, FOCUS, VIDEO, AUTORUN, or a file open in the STUDIO/Files viewer). Captures the on-screen image exactly as shown, with the applied stretch / white-balance / stacking. Use this whenever the user points at what's on screen without naming a source — 'this', 'what I'm looking at', 'the current view/panel', 'the image on screen' — or when you don't know which panel they're on. The image is attached right after this call; give a short verdict tailored to that panel (focus/HFR & star shape for FOCUS; framing, depth & gradients for LIVE/PREVIEW; trailing for tracking) plus any next step. If it reports no image is displayed, tell the user to switch to an imaging panel.

tools.name: get_studio_stats
tools.description: Summarise the captured-frame library: how many light frames are indexed, total integration time (hours), and how many distinct targets/filters. Use to answer 'how much did I capture' or before grading/stacking. Only counts frames the library has indexed; call refresh_library first if the user just captured and nothing shows up.

tools.name: refresh_library
tools.description: Re-scan the image output folder so newly captured frames appear in the library before you list/grade/stack them. Returns immediately; the scan runs in the background. Use it once when a just-finished session isn't showing up in list_frames or get_studio_stats.

tools.name: list_frames
tools.description: Browse the captured-frame library. Filter by type (LIGHT/DARK/FLAT/BIAS/MASTERLIGHT), filter name, target, and an ISO date window (dateFrom/dateTo compare against each frame's DATE-OBS, e.g. '2026-07-04'). Returns rows with id, path, fileName, target, filter, exposureSec, gain, and dateObs, newest first. Use it to see what was shot last night (type 'LIGHT' with a date window) or to find a specific master (type 'MASTERLIGHT'). To stack the BEST subs, don't hand this list to integrate directly — grade it first with grade_frames.

type.description: Frame type, e.g. LIGHT, MASTERLIGHT, DARK, FLAT, BIAS. Omit for all.

filter.description: Filter name, e.g. Ha, L, R. Omit for all.

target.description: Object name as stored in the FITS OBJECT header. Omit for all.

dateFrom.description: ISO date/time lower bound on DATE-OBS, e.g. '2026-07-04' or '2026-07-04T18:00:00'.

dateTo.description: ISO date/time upper bound on DATE-OBS.

tools.name: grade_frames
tools.description: Measure and rank a set of light frames by quality (star count + median HFR) and pick the best for stacking. Pass either explicit framePaths, or a library query (type defaults to LIGHT; filter/target/date window like list_frames) and it grades everything that matches. This is how you honour 'the best frames': grade first, then feed the returned `selected` paths to integrate_frames. Runs as a background job (star-detecting a whole night takes a while); the result comes back after it finishes with `results` (every frame's stars/hfr/score/keep, best first), `selected` (the keeper paths, ranked) and `selectedCount`. Choose the keep rule: keepBest N for a fixed count, hfrTolerancePct to keep everything within N% of the sharpest sub, or neither for a sensible default (within 20% of the best HFR and at least half the median star count).

framePaths.description: Explicit frame paths to grade. Omit to grade the library query below instead.

type.description: Frame type when querying the library (defaults to LIGHT).

filter.description: Filter name to restrict to (library query).

target.description: Target/object name to restrict to (library query).

dateFrom.description: ISO lower bound on DATE-OBS (library query), e.g. last night's date.

dateTo.description: ISO upper bound on DATE-OBS (library query).

limit.description: Max frames to grade from the library query (default 500).

keepBest.description: Keep exactly the N highest-scoring frames.

hfrTolerancePct.description: Keep every frame within this percent of the best HFR (ignored when keepBest is set).

tools.name: integrate_frames
tools.description: Align and stack (integrate) a set of already-captured light frames into one master light FITS. Pass the frame paths in framePaths (need at least 2) — typically the `selected` paths from grade_frames. Pick an integration method: SigmaClippedMean (default, rejects outliers like planes/satellites), Mean, or Median. Non-destructive: it writes a new master_light file and does not touch the subs or move any hardware. Runs as a background job; the result comes back when done with `stage` ('done' or 'error'), `outputPath` of the new master, `combined` (frames stacked), `dropped` (failed alignment) and `totalExposureSec`. After it finishes, call refresh_library then list_frames (type 'MASTERLIGHT') to locate the master, and preview_frame to show it. drizzleScale 2/3 upsamples for undersampled, well-dithered data (leave at 1 unless the user asks).

framePaths.description: Paths of the light frames to stack (>= 2). Usually grade_frames' selected list.

drizzleScale.description: 1 = native resolution; 2/3 = drizzle onto a finer grid (undersampled + dithered data only).

tools.name: preview_frame
tools.description: Fetch a library frame (by its numeric id from list_frames) as an auto-stretched image and inspect it — the frame is attached right after this call so you can look at it directly. Use it to show and assess a stacked master after integrate_frames (find its id via list_frames type 'MASTERLIGHT'), or to eyeball any indexed sub. Give a short verdict (depth, gradients, star shape, framing) and any next step.

tools.name: stop_live_stack
tools.description: Stop the running live (EAA) capture loop. MUTATES: ends the running session. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: dither_now
tools.description: Ask the guider to dither now (small random nudge so hot pixels/walking noise average out across subs). MUTATES: moves the mount slightly via the guider. Only inside an approved plan.

pixels.description: Dither amplitude in guide-camera pixels (optional; uses the guider default when omitted).

tools.name: stop_guiding
tools.description: Stop autoguiding. MUTATES: ends guiding on the running session. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: park_mount
tools.description: Park the telescope mount (moves it to its park position and stops tracking — the safe end-of-night state). MUTATES: moves the mount. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: unpark_mount
tools.description: Unpark the telescope mount so it can slew and track again. MUTATES: enables mount motion. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: stop_plan
tools.description: Stop the running multi-target night plan (PLAN mode). MUTATES: aborts the automated session. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: stop_sequence
tools.description: Stop the running capture sequence. MUTATES: aborts the running session. Only inside an approved plan.

tools.name: read_logs
tools.description: Read the Polaris application log (newest entries) to diagnose a problem. Filter by minimum level (info|warn|error), source, or a text search. Use this FIRST when the user reports something broke, a device misbehaved, or the app crashed.

level.description: Minimum level: info, warn, or error.

source.description: Filter by log source, e.g. server, http, link.

search.description: Only entries whose message contains this text.

tools.name: get_studio_root
tools.description: Get the Studio root (base image directory) so you know where captures live before browsing with list_dir.

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List the files and folders in a directory on the Polaris host, to find logs, config or image files to inspect. Use get_studio_root first to find where captures live.

path.description: Absolute directory path on the host.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file (config, log, script) on the Polaris host, up to a size cap. Binary files and files holding secrets (profiles, passwords, certificates) are refused. Use to inspect configuration or on-disk logs during debugging.

path.description: Absolute file path on the host.

tools.name: get_fits_headers
tools.description: Read the FITS header cards of an image file (exposure, gain, filter, temperature, WCS, etc.) to diagnose capture or plate-solve issues.

path.description: Absolute path to a .fits/.fit file on the host.
